title: a soft-deleted customer tries to sign up again, and the unique constraint remembers her

steps.note: customers with a deleted_at column: NULL means live.

steps.sql: SELECT id, email, deleted_at FROM customers ORDER BY id
UPDATE customers SET deleted_at = '2026-03-10 09:00+00' WHERE email = 'ada@example.com'
steps.note: Ada closes her account. nothing is deleted: the row gets a timestamp.

steps.sql: SELECT id, email, deleted_at FROM customers ORDER BY id
INSERT INTO customers (email, name) VALUES ('ada@example.com', 'Ada Lovelace')
steps.note: a month later Ada signs up again. UNIQUE (email) still sees the deleted row, and refuses.

error.message: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "customers_email_key"

steps.sql:
ALTER TABLE customers DROP CONSTRAINT customers_email_key;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX customers_email_live ON customers (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
steps.note: the fix: uniqueness only among live rows, a partial unique index.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO customers (email, name) VALUES ('ada@example.com', 'Ada Lovelace')
steps.note: the same sign-up now works: the old row is outside the index.

steps.sql: SELECT id, email, deleted_at FROM customers ORDER BY id
steps.note: two rows for ada@example.com, one deleted, one live.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO customers (email, name) VALUES ('ada@example.com', 'Ada again')
steps.note: and the rule still holds where it matters: two live rows with one email are refused.

error.message: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "customers_email_live"
